content.title: Tax Day is near. What to know about deadlines, extensions, refunds
content.text: April 8, 2026, 7:21 a.m. ETThe deadline to file taxes with the IRS is April 15, unless an extension is requested.Tax brackets are adjusted annually by the IRS to account for inflation.Taxpayers can file for an extension by April 15, which moves the filing deadline to October 15.Failing to file on time can result in a penalty of 5% of the tax due for each month the return is late.The April 15 tax deadline is quickly approaching, which means you might want to get your paperwork submitted to the Internal Revenue Service.Here's what to know about filing your taxes, and how to get an extension if you need one.What is the deadline to file taxes?Taxes must be filed by Wednesday, April 15, per the IRS, unless you file for an extension.Did your tax bracket change this year?This year's tax season will have slightly different brackets, according to TaxFoundation.org, which the IRS does annually to prevent "bracket creep," or when taxpayers are pushed into a higher bracket without any real change to their income or buying power due to inflation.For people filing as single individuals, the tax brackets in 2025 are:10% is $0 to $12,40012% is $12,401 to $50,40022% is $50,401 to $105,70024% is $105,701 to $201,77532% is $201,776 to $256,22535% is $256,226 to $640,60037% is $640,601 or moreIf you're filing a joint income, the tax brackets in 2025 are:10% is $0 to $24,80012% is $24,801 to $100,80022% is $100,801 to $211,40024% is $211,401 to $403,55032% is $403,551 to $512,45035% is $512,451 to $768,70037% is $768,701 or moreIf you're filing as head of household, the tax brackets in 2025 are:10% is $0 to $17,70012% is $17,701 to $67,45022% is $67,451 to $105,70024% is $105,701 to $201,77532% is $201,776 to $256,20035% is $256,201 to $640,60037% is $640,601 or moreWhat is the IRS deadline to file for a tax extension?The deadline to file for an extension is also April 15, according to the IRS, giving taxpayers until Oct. 15 to file without penalties. You still must pay any taxes owed by April 15, however, and the extension only applies to filing a tax return.What happens if I miss the filing deadline?If you fail to file or don't pay your federal tax return on time, the standard penalty is 5% of any tax due for every month the return is late, up to 25% of the unpaid balance.If you file for an extension, however, you face a much smaller monthly penalty of 0.5% of any unpaid amount.How do I request an extension to file taxes with the IRS? See extension deadline in KentuckyYou can request an extension with the IRS online or by mail by filing Form 4868.Those who file a federal extension by April 15, 2026, will receive a six-month extension for Kentucky state returns, with a deadline of Oct. 15, 2026.Is it free to file an extension on taxes?There's no penalty for filing a tax extension with the IRS, but not paying the full amount owed can lead to charges on the unpaid balance.Where's my refund? How to check with the IRSAfter you file, visit the IRS online at "Where's My Refund?" (irs.gov/refunds) or at the IRS2Go mobile app to get the latest details about your current tax return and refund. Here's when you can begin checking:24 hours after e-filing the current year's return.Three or four days after e-filing a prior tax year.Four weeks after mailing a paper return.What time does the IRS usually update 'Where's my refund?'The agency's "Where's My Refund?" portal is refreshed each morning, usually between the hours of 4 and 5 a.m., according to the IRS.How to check your tax refund status in KentuckyKentucky taxpayers can find out if the Department of Revenue has initiated their refund process at refund.ky.gov. You will have to enter your social security number and the exact refund amount.You can also speak with an examiner about a prior year's or amended refund by calling 502-564-4581.When will I receive my tax refund in Kentucky?The Kentucky Department of Revenue says e-filed returns will take 4-6 weeks and paper returns will take 10-14.John Tufts covers trending news for IndyStar and Midwest Connect.
